title: Local Privacy-First Document Classification
business: Legal firms handling sensitive client discovery documents that cannot be uploaded to third-party cloud APIs.
problem: High latency and strict data residency requirements prevent the use of external LLM services for automated document categorization.
solution: Deploying llama.cpp locally allows the firm to run quantized models on internal hardware, ensuring data never leaves the secure perimeter while maintaining high inference speed.
steps: Compile llama.cpp from source to ensure compatibility with local hardware architectures like AVX or Metal.
Download a GGUF-formatted model optimized for document classification tasks.
Apply integer quantization to the model weights to fit the model within existing local RAM or VRAM constraints.
Initialize the llama-server to expose an OpenAI-compatible REST API for internal document processing scripts.
Route document text streams through the local server for automated tagging and metadata extraction.
outcome: The firm achieves full data sovereignty with sub-second inference latency, enabling real-time document triage without external network dependencies.
limitation: Quantization reduces model precision, which can lead to subtle degradation in classification accuracy; this is verified by comparing output confidence scores against a baseline unquantized model.
